The Cislunar Gateway International Habitat (I-HAB) is ESAs contribution of an infrastructure element supporting the Gateway with full crew habitability and utilization requirements from 2025. 
The I-HAB includes contributions from USA, Japan and Canada. The Cislunar Gateway is a multi-element infrastructure designed to support both robotic and human exploration of cis-lunar space and act as a basecamp for sustained lunar exploration. The Lunar Gateway is smaller than the ISS and will require less launches for its assembly. It is intended to be occupied by a crew of up to four astronauts for periods ranging from two weeks to two months, but otherwise operates as a robotic spacecraft.
The objective of the present procurement is the selection of the contractor for Fluidic Ground Support Equipment for I-HAB in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment are part of the equipment belonging to the I-HAB Gateway module.
 The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment are the needed items to perform the fluidic checks on all fluidic components and systems of the I-HAB module.
They will allow the fluidic qualification and acceptance tests on all ducts, tubes, pumps, radiators, cold plates valves and circuit partial and complete that will be installed inside to the I-HAB module.
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment will permit the following activities and tests:
	- Liquid filling HFE 7200, Water/Glycol mixture solution, Water etc.
-	Flushing with gas and liquids
-	Test support with the I-HAB thermal control system (providing fluids at required pressure, temperature and flow)
-	Proof pressure tests with gas and liquids
-	Leakage test with tracing gas (helium) or through the pressure decay methods, monitoring the internal pressure behavior
-	Gas filling, Nitrogen helium, Oxygen 
The Fluidic Ground Support Equipment is expected to be safe and in according to the European and USA rules for dedicated fluidic equipment and servicer Notwithstanding the complete list of countries identified in the Special Provision for visibility purposes, the ITT letter of invitation will contain a dedicated set of geographical return requirements/targets to be considered.
Further information concerning the I-HAB can be found on the Agencys website here:https://www.esa.int/Science_Exploration/Human_and_Robotic_Exploration/Gateway_to_the_Moon
